title: Sawin’s totally real towers
summary: Sawin’s arithmetic construction produces totally real fields of increasing degree with bounded root discriminant and infinitely many completely split primes. This library formalizes that construction in Lean.
overview: A totally real number field has only real embeddings. Its root discriminant, the absolute discriminant raised to the reciprocal of the degree, measures discriminant growth on a common scale across different degrees. Sawin’s tower construction keeps this quantity bounded as the degree grows, while one fixed infinite set of rational primes splits completely throughout the tower. Such fields provide the arithmetic input for constructions in the unit-distance problem.

The library formalizes this arithmetic construction using pro-2 Galois groups, controlled ramification and Golod–Shafarevich estimates. Its infinite-prime conclusion is the tower statement in Proposition 2.3 of [Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695). The development also includes discriminant estimates and Shafarevich’s relation-rank bound.
scopeNote: The main endpoint is an arithmetic existence theorem used in Sawin's unit-distance work; this is not a formalization of the entire unit-distance disproof. The bound 255255 is not claimed to be optimal. The separately listed Shafarevich theorem assumes an odd prime and must not be substituted for the pro-2 arithmetic used in the tower construction.

entries.title: Sawin’s theorem on totally real towers and split primes
entries.summary: A single infinite set of primes splits completely in totally real fields with uniformly bounded root discriminant.
statement: There are a real constant $B$ and an infinite set $Q$ of primes, all congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, such that for every $N$ there is a totally real number field $F$ with $$[F:\mathbb Q]\ge N,\qquad |\operatorname{disc}(F)|^{1/[F:\mathbb Q]}\le B,$$ and every $q\in Q$ splits completely in $F$.

The implementation chooses $B=255255$. Its explicit splitting conclusion supplies $[F:\mathbb Q]$ distinct maximal ideals of $\mathcal O_F$ containing $q$. For a rational prime in a number field, this maximal number of distinct primes above $q$ expresses complete splitting.
history: This infinite-prime formulation is Proposition 2.3 of the joint paper Remarks on the disproof of the unit distance conjecture. It uses the Frobenius-cutting method of Hajir, Maire, and Ramakrishna. Sawin’s single-author paper gives related arithmetic ingredients for the unit-distance application; its formulation and the joint paper’s proposition should be distinguished.

entries.title: Shafarevich’s relation-rank bound for odd primes
entries.summary: Degree-two continuous cohomology of the maximal everywhere-unramified pro-p group is finite and arithmetically bounded.
statement: Let $F$ be a number field and $p$ an odd prime. Let $G$ be its maximal everywhere-unramified pro-$p$ Galois group, and let $d(G)$ be its finite topological generator rank. Write $r_1,r_2$ for its numbers of real and complex places and put $\delta=1$ if $F$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity, and $\delta=0$ otherwise.

The theorem proves that $H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\mathbb F_p)$ is finite-dimensional and $$\dim_{\mathbb F_p}H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\mathbb F_p)\le d(G)+(r_1+r_2-1)+\delta.$$ The coefficient module is the trivial module.
history: Shafarevich’s 1963 paper studies extensions with prescribed ramification and underlies the arithmetic relation estimates used in class field tower theory. Golod and Shafarevich’s subsequent infinitude argument shows why these bounds matter: controlling relations relative to generators can force an unramified tower to continue indefinitely.
